<RecipePage recipeId="validate-and-publish-skill">

<RecipeSection label="Problem">

You have a local SKILL.md file and want to publish it to your Glean instance. Before adding version management or GitHub imports, start by validating the file, creating a skill, and checking that you can retrieve it. This quickstart uses the official TypeScript API client to complete that workflow, then deletes the test skill. It verifies that the downloaded SKILL.md matches the uploaded file byte for byte, without extracting files to disk or executing the skill.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeArchitecture />

<RecipePrereqs />

<RecipeSteps />

<RecipeSection label="Validate before creating a skill">

Call validate first and stop on any error. Validation itself never creates or updates a skill.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Use a new name">

The API can add a version when a name already exists. Use an unused name and avoid concurrent runs with that name. Creation is not retried automatically. If creation times out, inspect your instance before running it again; a skill may have been saved without returning its ID.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Treat content as untrusted">

Limit the ZIP download to 10 MiB. Read its single regular root SKILL.md in memory, with decompression bounded by the uploaded file size. Require a valid checksum and exact file bytes. Do not extract files to disk or execute retrieved content.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Delete by captured ID only">

Deletion is permanent. Clean up only the new skill identified by the create response, never a name-search result. If the API returns a later version, stop without deleting it. If deletion fails, the command reports the remaining ID and exits with an error.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Experimental API">

The scaffold opts in with includeExperimental, but the Skills endpoints may still be unavailable on a tenant or change before general availability.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Publishing is not execution">

The API stores and distributes skill bundles. This quickstart verifies the bytes of a single uploaded SKILL.md, not multi-file bundles or skill execution. It does not run the skill or test how an agent host interprets it.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Sign-in permissions vary by instance">

Your instance must allow the SKILLS scope. If OAuth is unavailable, use a user-scoped token with that scope. The newer skills:read and skills:write scopes are not supported yet.

</RecipeSection>

<TakeItFurther>

- Use the skill-publishing-pipeline recipe to publish another version, inspect a specific version, and examine a downloaded archive safely.
- Use the GitHub import recipe when the source of truth is a public repository rather than a local SKILL.md.
- After you can create and retrieve a skill, use its ID to explore version management and enabling or disabling it.

</TakeItFurther>
